# `Q-12-7` — `template:` Requires `type: custom`

> `template:` was set but `type:` is not `custom`; the built-in
> template for the declared type is used instead.

## What this means

A listing's `template:` key points at a custom template file
(a doctemplate — see the [Listings guide](/guides/projects/listings.qmd#custom-templates)) that Quarto uses to render
each item. The key only has an effect when `type: custom` —
otherwise the listing uses one of the four built-in templates
(`default`, `grid`, `table`, ...) and there is no point at which
the custom template would be consulted.

When you set `template:` on a non-custom type, Quarto warns and
ignores the template — the built-in for the declared type
renders the listing.

## Why this happens

Two common causes:

- **Migration from Quarto 1**, where some templates were
  attached to non-custom types in a way Quarto 2 does not
  preserve.
- **A copy-paste mistake** that combined fields from two
  listings without keeping the matching `type:`.

## How to fix

Either set `type: custom` (so the template is used) or remove
the `template:` line (if you wanted the built-in for the
declared type all along).

## Related

- `Q-12-14` — the reverse: `type: custom` was set but no
  `template:` path was given.
- `Q-12-8` — `template:` set, but the file at that path could
  not be read.
